title: The Face Beside the Furnace
paras: At an industrial arts museum, sculptor Amara Sen investigated whether documentary context could alter the apparent emotion of a portrait. Her bronze represented an anonymous foundry worker whose [[countenance|countenance]] had been deliberately rendered ambiguous. Before casting, technicians recorded the crucible’s [[tare|tare]], weighed a single [[ingot|ingot]], and retained the [[slag|slag]] separated during melting for an accompanying display.

Sen commissioned a theatrical specialist to [[hairdress|hairdress]] a wig for the model, following an archival photograph. Behind the finished portrait stood a drawing of the foundry’s [[sluice|sluice]], which had regulated water entering its wheelhouse. These elements remained identical across two viewing sessions; only the explanatory panel changed. Eighty adult volunteers were randomly assigned to see one version.

The first panel described technical processes; the second reproduced a wage ledger, a [[promissory|promissory]] note issued instead of cash, and a rule making permission to leave work the proprietor’s sole [[prerogative|prerogative]]. It also quoted a physician’s attribution of workers’ distress to ‘[[neurosis|neurosis]]’, explicitly identifying this as historical terminology. Viewers then rated the face without being told that another panel existed.

Those given employment records rated the unchanged expression as markedly more anxious, although both groups judged its craftsmanship similarly. Sen resisted claiming that the experiment recovered the worker’s actual feelings: it demonstrated an interpretative effect, not historical access to a mind. Her final installation therefore presented both panels together, alongside a declaration that personal freedom is [[inalienable|inalienable]]. The bronze had not changed; the evidence surrounding it had made neutrality harder to sustain.
zh: 在一座工业艺术博物馆里，雕塑家阿玛拉·森研究了一个问题：文献背景能否改变观众从肖像中感受到的情绪？她的青铜像表现的是一位无名铸造工人，其神情被刻意塑造得模棱两可。浇铸之前，技术人员记录了坩埚的皮重，称量了一块金属锭，并保留了熔炼过程中分离出的炉渣，用于配套展陈。
森请一位舞台造型专家参照档案照片，为模特所戴的假发做造型。完成的肖像后方摆着一幅铸造厂闸控水道的图纸；这条水道曾用于调节流入水轮机房的水量。在两场观看活动中，这些元素完全相同，变化的只有说明展板。八十名成年志愿者被随机分配，各自观看其中一个版本。
第一块展板介绍技术工艺；第二块则复制展示了一份工资账册、一张代替现金发放的付款承诺票据，以及一条将离岗决定权交给厂主的规定。它还引用了一位医生将工人痛苦归因于“神经症”的说法，并明确指出这是历史用语。随后，观众在不知道还存在另一块展板的情况下，对面部表情作出评分。
看到雇佣记录的观众认为，同一副表情显得明显更加焦虑，不过两组对雕塑技艺的评价相近。森没有据此宣称实验还原了工人的真实感受：它揭示的是解读方式受到影响，而不是让人得以进入历史人物的内心。因此，她在最终展陈中同时呈现了两块展板，并附上一份宣言，声明人身自由不可剥夺或转让。青铜像并未改变；周围的证据却使中立的解读更难维持。

q.s: Sen deliberately gave the worker an unmistakably anxious expression.
q.why: 首段说明神情被刻意塑造得模棱两可。

q.s: Most volunteers had previously visited exhibitions about industrial labour.
q.why: 文章未提及志愿者以往的观展经历。

q.s: The two groups gave similar assessments of the portrait's craftsmanship.
q.why: 末段明确说两组对雕塑技艺的评价相近。
